completion_conditions: The bootstrapped first-task lock default covers repository-root files as well as nested files.
The everything-lock conflicts with a root-file lock such as path:package.json, closing the serialization gap the same pattern caused.
A regression test binds the real bootstrap default (not a copy of the literal) and fails when the default is reverted.

decisions: THE DEFECT, MEASURED. `path:**/*` requires a literal "/" under fnmatch. In-worktree 2026-08-22: files_outside_locks(['package.json','tsconfig.json','.gitignore','src/env.d.ts'], ['path:**/*']) -> ['package.json','tsconfig.json','.gitignore']; the same call with ['path:**'] -> []. Against the exact six paths from shiki-atlas PR #2 plus one nested file, the shipped default blocks all six root files and the fix blocks none.

THE SECOND FACE, NOT IN THE REPORT. The same gap breaks conflict detection, not just coverage. Measured: locks_overlap('path:**/*','path:package.json') is False, while locks_overlap('path:**','path:package.json') is True. A bootstrap task holding the everything-lock therefore did NOT conflict with a second task declaring path:package.json, so both could claim the file concurrently and active_lock_conflicts stayed silent. Against directory locks the two forms behave identically (both overlap path:tests/**, path:scripts/mergegate_check.py and shiki:governance), so this defect was invisible except at repository root. One character fixes both faces.

SCOPE, AUDITED. grep for the lock idiom across scripts/, docs/, templates, .github/ and .shiki/ returns exactly two occurrences, both in scripts/shiki_bootstrap.py: the interactive fallback at line 320 and the non-interactive fallback at line 325. The `--lock` argparse entries (shiki_cli.py:162, :354) carry no help text naming a default, no document states one, and no test pins the literal - scripts/test_shiki_start.sh:125 passes "path:src/start/*" explicitly and so never exercises the default. The fix surface is therefore those two lines plus a regression test, with no doc or template alignment needed.

BINDING THE PAIR. The default is promoted to a module-level DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS in shiki_bootstrap.py and both call sites resolve through it, so tests/test_lock_matching.py can import the real default instead of restating the literal. This follows the binder convention stated in tests/test_paired_invariants.py: where nothing binds two artifacts that must agree, a break is silent. Each coverage assertion is paired with a divergence test that feeds the old pattern to the same helper, proving the suite detects the regression rather than merely passing on today's tree.

RISK IS LOW AND THE ARCHITECTURE GATE IS NOT TRIGGERED. Two default-value lines, one constant with its rationale comment, and one test class: no schema, workflow, public API, auth, migration or infrastructure surface; under 100 net new lines in a core module; no new files; two files touched. Low and medium both take the autonomous SADR-0008/SADR-0009 merge path, so this classification does not change the loop route.

MEASURED GREEN BEFORE FREEZE. The candidate change was applied in the planning worktree purely to measure lock sufficiency, then reverted so this contract registers no implementation. Results: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> Ran 1176 tests, OK; `python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .` -> Shiki validation passed; scripts/test_shiki_start.sh, test_shiki_init.sh and test_shiki_control_plane.sh all PASS. Red proof: reverting DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS to ['path:**/*'] fails exactly 3 tests in the new class, and the failure message names scripts/shiki_bootstrap.py DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS as the fix.

LOCK SUFFICIENCY. MUST-CHANGE is scripts/shiki_bootstrap.py and tests/test_lock_matching.py, and the measured green run changed nothing else. MUST-NOT-BREAK is the full Python suite, validate_shiki and every scripts/test_shiki_*.sh, all of which are verification commands rather than lock entries. The two locks are therefore sufficient and no lock-widening amendment should be needed.
grill_with_docs.source: Claude Code planning session 2026-08-22 in worktree sleepy-chatelet-e30d87, from an operator bug report with a reproduction; every claim below re-measured independently in that worktree rather than taken from the report.

non_goals: Loosening files_outside_locks, path_matches_lock, path_lock_patterns or any other matching semantics. The glob behavior is correct; only the default pattern was wrong. Measured: path_lock_patterns already expands a trailing "/*" to "/**", but that expansion cannot rescue "**/*" because the resulting "**/**" still requires a separator.

Adding a warning when a path:**/* lock is declared by hand elsewhere. Raised in the report as a "consider"; it would touch lock acquisition and validation surfaces outside this slice. Deferred as a follow-up, not decided here.

Backfilling existing .shiki/tasks records. Audited 2026-08-22: no tracked mirror record declares the pattern, and mirror rewrites are a migration-mode concern (see the byte-boundary constraint in SADR-0016's mirror-identity rules).

Revisiting SADR-0016's lock-granularity planning rule that a lock must not be a directory glob over a shared namespace when files are nameable at plan time. A bootstrapped first task has no plan-time file list, which is why it has a fallback at all.
outcome: A repository bootstrapped by `shiki start` gets a first-task lock that actually means "everything". Measured 2026-08-22: with the shipped default `path:**/*`, files_outside_locks(['package.json','tsconfig.json','.gitignore','src/env.d.ts']) returns the three repository-root files, because fnmatch requires a literal "/" to satisfy `**/*`; with `path:**` it returns []. Live consequence on mizutani-140/shiki-atlas PR #2: MergeGate emitted six "Changed file X is outside declared task locks" reasons for .gitignore, astro.config.mjs, package-lock.json, package.json, tsconfig.json and vitest.config.ts, every one of them a root-level file a normal first slice legitimately creates, forcing the operator to hand-edit task.locks and re-run `shiki lock acquire` on the very first task of a new project.

spec_freeze.source: Operator approved the drafted requirements in the Claude Code planning session on 2026-08-22, answering the Spec Freeze question with 'Approve - freeze and register' after reviewing the measured defect, the previously unreported conflict-detection face, the audited two-occurrence fix surface, the DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS binder design call, and the low risk classification. Recorded by the planner on the operator's instruction; the approval is the operator's.

acceptance_checks: scripts/shiki_bootstrap.py defines a module-level DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS equal to ["path:**"].
Both first-task lock fallbacks in scripts/shiki_bootstrap.py resolve through DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS, and the literal "path:**/*" does not appear anywhere in the file.
files_outside_locks(["src/env.d.ts","a/b/c/deep.ts",".github/workflows/x.yml"], DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS) == [] - nested coverage is not regressed.
A divergence test asserts files_outside_locks(["package.json","tsconfig.json",".gitignore"], ["path:**/*"]) still returns all three, proving the coverage assertion discriminates.
any(locks_overlap(lock, "path:package.json") for lock in DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS) is True.
A divergence test asserts locks_overlap("path:**/*", "path:package.json") is False.
The new tests live in tests/test_lock_matching.py and fail when DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS is reverted to ["path:**/*"]; the failure message names scripts/shiki_bootstrap.py DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
tasks.scope:
In scripts/shiki_bootstrap.py, introduce a module-level DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS = ["path:**"] carrying a comment that states why `path:**/*` is wrong (fnmatch requires a literal "/", so it matches src/env.d.ts but not package.json), and resolve both first-task lock fallbacks through it - the interactive one at line 320 and the non-interactive one at line 325. Remove the `"path:**/*"` literal from the file entirely.

In tests/test_lock_matching.py, add a test class that imports DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS from shiki_bootstrap and asserts against the real default rather than a restated literal. It must cover: repository-root files are inside the default; nested files are still inside; the everything-lock conflicts with path:package.json; and the source file no longer contains the broken literal. Pair the two behavioral assertions with divergence tests that feed ['path:**/*'] to the same helpers and assert the old failing results, so the suite proves it detects the regression instead of merely passing today.

Change nothing in scripts/shiki_locks.py. The glob semantics are correct - only the default pattern was wrong - and loosening the matcher is a stated non-goal.

REPRODUCIBILITY - what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: an operator runs `shiki start` on a new project, the first slice creates package.json / tsconfig.json / .gitignore, and MergeGate blocks the PR with one "Changed file X is outside declared task locks" reason per root file. Observed live on mizutani-140/shiki-atlas PR #2 with six such reasons. The declared lock was intended to mean "everything".
  Root cause: scripts/shiki_bootstrap.py defaults task locks to ["path:**/*"] in two places. Under fnmatch that pattern requires a literal "/", so it matches nested paths only.
  Second, unreported face: locks_overlap('path:**/*','path:package.json') is False, so the everything-lock also failed to serialize against a root-file lock.
  Why it was silent: no test pinned the default (test_shiki_start.sh passes an explicit lock), no doc stated it, and against directory locks the broken and correct forms behave identically.
  Reproducible when: DEFAULT_FIRST_TASK_LOCKS is reverted to ["path:**/*"], which must fail the new tests.
